cues.en: In advocating for low-density living, people often contrast their peaceful suburbs and quiet small towns with the crowds and chaos of downtown, especially if they live close to a big city with a major central business district that's a regional destination. In this video, we want to propose that people from outside of cities tend to have a skewed perception of urban living and density because their experience with city life is mostly with downtown in the most literal sense. When they go to the city, they're commuting to a job in the financial district.
cues.zh: 在提倡低密度居住时，人们常把宁静的郊区和安静的小镇，与市中心的拥挤和混乱作对比，特别是当他们住在一个拥有大型中央商务区（区域级目的地）的大城市附近时。在这期视频中，我们想提出一个观点：城外的人往往对城市生活和密度有着片面的看法，因为他们对城市生活的体验，大多仅限于字面意义上的“市中心”。当他们进城时，他们是通勤去金融区上班，

cues.en: or they're going to an event in a downtown stadium or convention center, typically with lots of other suburbanites and out-of-towners. They're generally not visiting the countless dense residential neighborhoods outside of downtown, where most urbanites actually live and spend most of their time. The disproportionate amount of space taken by the Central Business District, in people's perception of city life, is something we've seen from other people, but also experienced ourselves. We both grew up well outside of cities.
cues.zh: 或是去市中心的体育场或会议中心参加活动，身边的也大多是其他郊区居民和外地人。他们通常不会去逛市中心以外无数密集居民区，而那才是大多数城市居民真正生活和大部分时间所在的地方。中央商务区在人们对城市生活的认知中所占比例过大，这种现象我们不仅在他人身上见过，自己也深有体会。我们俩都是在远离城市的地方长大的，

cues.en: and for quite a few years didn't have a great sense of what it was actually like to live in one. When I first moved to Toronto for grad school, I talked to someone about an apartment opportunity in a house, and I remember asking them whether they could see the CN Tower from their street. They found that funny, because the CN Tower is just not something they think about on a daily basis, but the downtown landmarks were such a big part of my perception of the city. After moving to a different apartment nearby, I realized just how much downtown actually feels like a different world.
cues.zh: 而且有好些年对在城里生活的真正体验并不太了解。当我最初去多伦多读研时，我曾向人打听过一套合租独立屋里的房源，我记得当时还问过对方从他们那条街上能不能看到 CN 塔。他们觉得这问题挺好笑，因为日常生活里他们根本不会去想 CN 塔，但市中心的地标在我对这座城市的印象中却占据了很大一部分。搬到附近另一间公寓后，我才意识到市中心给人的感觉究竟有多像另一个世界，

cues.en: even though it was still kind of cool that you could sometimes see the CN Tower. And this was near the University of Toronto, which is only two or three kilometers from downtown. There are lots of other dense urban neighborhoods further away that feel even more removed from downtown. We actually understand the aversion that many people have to downtown living. In both Toronto and Montreal, we often went downtown for things we needed or just to explore, but it wouldn't be our first choice for where to wake up every day.
cues.zh: 尽管偶尔能看到 CN 塔依然挺酷的。这地方还在多伦多大学附近，距离市中心也就两三公里。还有许多距离更远、密度也很高的高密度居民区，感觉与市中心更加脱节。其实我们完全理解很多人对住在市中心的抗拒。在多伦多和蒙特利尔时，我们常去市中心办事或单纯闲逛，但绝不会把那里作为每天醒来的首选居住地。

cues.en: Many people enjoy the unparalleled convenience, but we find it can be overwhelming when you combine the residents, commuters, tourists, and other visitors, including people coming to the central city just to be loud and express their views, like protesters and preachers. There also usually isn't as much quiet, calming space immediately accessible, whether quiet streets or parks. Canadian downtowns don't have the associations with violence that many central cities in the US have.
cues.zh: 很多人喜欢那里无与伦比的便利，但我们觉得，当把居民、通勤者、游客和其他访客混在一起时，往往会让人有些喘不过气，这其中还包括专门跑到市中心来喧哗、表达观点的人，比如抗议者和传教士。此外，周边通常也没有那么多触手可及的安静惬意空间，不论是僻静的街道还是公园。加拿大的市中心倒还不像许多美国中心城区那样，总让人联想到暴力犯罪。

cues.en: But property crime can be an issue, and it's probably not a coincidence that the year we lived on the edge of downtown Toronto was the year one of our bikes got chopped up and stolen. It might seem funny that the people behind an urbanism channel aren't big proponents of quote-unquote downtown living. But the part of the city we're talking about, with the biggest concentration of residential density, office towers, and attractions for tourists and visitors, is actually pretty small. That's not what city life is for most people.
cues.zh: 但财产犯罪可能是个问题，我们住在多伦多市中心边缘的那一年，恰好有一辆自行车被拆了偷走，这大概不是巧合。一个城市主义频道的运营者不算所谓“市中心生活”的拥护者，这也许有点好笑。但我们说的这片区域——住宅密度、办公塔楼和游客景点最集中的地方——其实相当小。大多数人的城市生活并不是那样的。

cues.en: You can live two or three kilometers away, sometimes even less, and have an entirely different experience. The two neighborhoods we have the most experience with, the Annex and Harvard Village area in Toronto, and the Plateau in Montreal, are good examples, but we could list dozens of other comparable neighborhoods, like the Golden Triangle in Ottawa and the West End in Vancouver. All of these areas are quite dense, housing four to eight times more people than a typical suburban neighborhood.
cues.zh: 你住在两三公里外，有时甚至更近，体验就可能完全不同。我们最熟悉的两个社区——多伦多的The Annex和Harvard Village一带，以及蒙特利尔的Plateau——就是很好的例子，但我们还能列出几十个类似社区，比如渥太华的Golden Triangle和温哥华的West End。这些地方都相当密集，居住人数是典型郊区的四到八倍。

cues.en: But to focus on the plateau and the annex, where we have the most experienced living, neither of these neighborhoods felt crowded, noisy, and overwhelming, in the way that the two cities downtown sometimes did. Both had lively commercial streets with bars, restaurants, and shops, and these could definitely get busy at times, but they were also balanced out by so many quiet residential streets that you could easily walk to or live on if you prefer. In both neighborhoods, we lived on residential streets two or three hundred meters from the main commercial streets.
cues.zh: 但聚焦我们住得最久的Plateau和The Annex，这两个社区都不像两座城市的市中心有时那样，让人感到拥挤、吵闹、压抑。两者都有热闹的商业街，有酒吧、餐厅和商店，这些地方有时确实很忙，但也被许多安静的住宅街平衡掉了；你如果愿意，很容易走到或住在这样的街上。在这两个社区，我们都住在离主要商业街两三百米的住宅街上。

cues.en: and basically did not encounter noise or commotion problems at all. Well, until the Montreal Canadiens made it to the Stanley Cup finals, and the entire city of Montreal went absolutely crazy, and a nearby apartment got gutted from a fire. Okay, that doesn't sound great, but you have to give Montreal some leeway for hockey. Aside from that, our experience living in these dense urban neighbourhoods was remarkably calm and peaceful, no less so than in the suburbs. In some ways, there was more peace and quiet.
cues.zh: 而且基本上完全没遇到噪音或骚动问题。好吧，直到蒙特利尔加拿大人队打进斯坦利杯决赛，整个蒙特利尔都彻底疯了，附近一间公寓还被火烧空了。好吧，这听起来不太好，但冰球这事你得给蒙特利尔一点宽容。除此之外，我们住在这些高密度城市社区的体验非常平静安宁，不比郊区差。某些方面还更安静。

cues.en: because suburban areas have their own noise issues, like large dogs, loud machinery like lawnmowers and leaf blowers, and the bigger, noisier cars and trucks that are more common in the suburbs. We've said that we prefer the environment of a dense residential neighborhood over downtown, which raises the question of whether that's a good reason to block new development in these neighborhoods to cap density and avoid becoming downtown. The annex in Toronto is always in the news trying to block development. Is that legitimate?
cues.zh: 因为郊区有自己的噪音问题，比如大狗、割草机和吹叶机这类吵闹机器，还有郊区更常见、更大更吵的汽车和卡车。我们说过，比起市中心，我们更喜欢高密度住宅社区的环境，这就引出一个问题：这是否是阻止这些社区新开发、限制密度、避免变成市中心的充分理由？多伦多的The Annex总因试图阻止开发而上新闻。这合理吗？

cues.en: They'll note that they're already fairly dense, which is true at least by suburban standards, but they have a very long way to go before they become downtown, and they're less dense than Montreal neighborhoods that we also find very calm. On top of this, downtown is far more than just residential density, unless you have the big amenities that draw people in from all over the region in the middle of your neighborhood, like stadiums and shopping malls and office towers. It's pretty unlikely that you'll end up with the same level of commotion.
cues.zh: 他们会说这里其实已经挺密集的了，按郊区标准来看确实如此，但离市中心那种程度还差得远，而且密度也比蒙特利尔那些同样很安静的街区要低。更重要的是，市中心可不仅意味着居住密度高，除非你的街区正中央有体育场、大型商场和写字楼这些能吸引全城人流的大型设施，否则几乎不可能搞得像市中心那么喧闹。

cues.en: Even small-scale amenities won't do that. We had a cafe, bookstore, small grocery store, and music conservatory in the middle of our residential neighborhood in Montreal, and it was pretty sweet. Finally, a big part of the commotion of downtown is all the cars driving through. Substantial car traffic adds stress and commotion to a place like almost nothing else, especially if there's honking. If a neighborhood minimizes that with traffic calming and pedestrian streets, and they prioritize accessibility through walking, cycling, and transit instead,
cues.zh: 即便是小型配套设施也不会造成这种喧闹。我们在蒙特利尔住的居民区中心，就有一家咖啡馆、书店、小杂货铺和一所音乐学院，生活别提有多惬意了。最后，市中心的大部分喧嚣都来自穿行的车辆。大量的车流给一个地方带来的压力和喧闹几乎是无与伦比的，特别是还有鸣笛声的时候。如果一个街区能通过交通安宁化设计和步行街将其降到最低，并优先保障步行、骑行和公交的便利性，

cues.en: They can house a lot more people while still providing a calm and relaxing environment. Changes like that could also be used to make actual downtown a more calming and relaxing place, even with large numbers of people, although that's a different video. Obviously not everyone has the same preferences and tolerances as us. Some people thrive in a bustling downtown environment, and other people want nothing more than to live in the middle of the woods far from anyone else. We just want to point out that a lot of people from outside the city, including us at one point,
cues.zh: 就能在容纳更多人口的同时，依然保持宁静惬意的环境。类似的改变也可以用来让真正的市中心变得更加安宁祥和，即便那里人口密集，不过这就扯远了，留在以后的视频里讲吧。当然，每个人的喜好和耐受度都不尽相同。有人在繁华喧嚣的市中心如鱼得水，也有人一心只想住进远离人烟的深山老林。我们只是想指出，许多非本地人——包括曾经的我们——

cues.en: Don't really know what it's like to live in a dense urban neighbourhood, because their main experience with a bigger, denser city is as a visitor, maybe coming in on a crowded highway and having trouble finding parking, then going to the downtown attractions at the same time as lots of other commuters, suburbanites, and visitors. These things are part of city life. Urbanites often go to these events too, but it's just one small slice of city life. Something really gets lost when we debate downtown living compared to suburban or small town living.
cues.zh: 并不真正了解住在高密度城市街区是什么体验，因为他们对大而密集的城市的了解主要来自游客视角，比如在拥堵的公路上开过来、到处找车位，然后和一大堆上班族、郊区居民及游客一起挤在市中心的景点里。这些确实是城市生活的一部分，城里人也经常参加这些活动，但这仅仅是城市生活的一个切片而已。当我们在争论住市中心好还是住郊区、小镇好时，往往忽略了一些重要的东西，

cues.en: because there's a wide range of possibilities in between. Thanks for watching through to the end of the video. Don't forget that dense living comes in many forms, and subscribe. A special thanks goes out to our supporters on Patreon.
cues.zh: 因为在这两者之间，其实还有非常广阔的折中可能。感谢大家把视频看到最后。别忘了，高密度居住其实有各种各样的形式，记得点击订阅哦。特别鸣谢我们在 Patreon 上的赞助者们。
